audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says Irelia's passive is an ARMOUR SHRED, five separate times: "before her passive shred stacks", "Stack her passive shred by Q-dashing... to shred your armor", "her level 1 pre-shred damage", "her shred is compounding", "compounding shred from a stacked passive", "shreds enough armor to punish your lack of mobility".
audit.why: Ionian Fervor grants stacking bonus ATTACK SPEED when Irelia strikes enemies with spells, and bonus on-hit damage at maximum stacks. It shreds nothing. This actively misdirects itemisation: a Tahm Kench who believes his armour is being stripped will buy more armour and stack HP, when the correct read is that her threat scales with attack speed and on-hit — which is what makes Thick Skin's grey-health banking work against her in the first place. The one place the file gets the mechanic right by accident is that passive stacks come off SPELLS, so 'stack it by Q-dashing through the wave' is correct.
audit.corrected: Ionian Fervor = stacking attack speed off spell hits, bonus on-hit damage at max stacks. No armour shred anywhere in the kit.
sources: champ-data/_kits/irelia.json — P Ionian Fervor: 'When Irelia strikes enemies with spells she gains stacking bonus Attack Speed. At maximum stacks she also gains bonus damage on hit.'

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says of the stun-into-Devour: "she cannot Riposte it and she cannot dash out".
audit.why: Riposte is Fiora's W. Irelia does not have it and never has. The entry has imported another champion's ability into the matchup. Irelia's W is Defiant Dance.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] claims Irelia will "Use W to block your empowered Devour damage burst so she takes the minimum and heals back immediately", and wants.you[1] calls her W a "burst-heal window".
audit.why: Two errors stacked on one ability, and the correction flips the matchup's key trade. Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage taken while charging — Devour deals MAGIC damage, so her W does not blunt your commit at all. And Defiant Dance has no healing whatsoever; Irelia's heal is Bladesurge (Q), which additionally refreshes its own cooldown against a Marked target or on a kill. So the real state of play is the opposite of what is written: her defensive cooldown is irrelevant against your ultimate, which is the strongest argument in the whole matchup for committing the three-stack stun.
audit.corrected: Defiant Dance cuts physical damage only and does nothing to Devour's magic damage. Her sustain is Bladesurge.
sources: champ-data/_kits/irelia.json — W Defiant Dance: 'She takes reduced physical damage during the charge'; Q Bladesurge: 'dashes forward to strike her target, healing herself. If the target is Marked or dies to Bladesurge, its cooldown refreshes'. champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — R Devour: 'dealing magic damage if they are an enemy'

audit.whatIsWrong: Vanguard's Edge is never mentioned anywhere in the entry, in either layer's prose. The full layer's 'Level 6 — Irelia' phase says only 'Irelia's ultimate changes the math too'.
audit.why: This is the flagged missing interaction and it is the most important single fact in the matchup for Tahm Kench specifically. Vanguard's Edge leaves a WALL that damages and slows anyone crossing it, and Tahm Kench has no dash in his kit — the only movement tool he owns is Abyssal Dive, which is a committal engage, not an escape. So her R does not just burst him, it removes his exit entirely. Flash has to be held for the wall, not saved for the damage.
audit.corrected: Vanguard's Edge walls off the retreat; with no dash, Flash is the wall answer.
sources: champ-data/_kits/irelia.json — R Vanguard's Edge: 'the blades form a wall that will damage and slow enemies that walk through it', flags terrain+slow. champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — kitFlags contain no dash. _missing-interactions.json rule terrain-cuts-retreat for tahmkench vs irelia

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags that the entry never names a single Irelia ability — it says only "her Q dash", "E stun", "her W", "her passive". Confirmed across all of spikes, wants, early, mid, late and whys.
audit.why: The full layer does name Flawless Duet, so a player reading both layers gets two different vocabularies for the same lane. Naming also carries mechanics the letters do not: Flawless Duet is two blades that CONVERGE, and the stun only lands on someone caught between them — which is a dodge instruction, not just a cooldown to count.
audit.corrected: Name Ionian Fervor, Bladesurge, Defiant Dance, Flawless Duet and Vanguard's Edge in the content layer.
sources: champ-data/_kits/irelia.json — E Flawless Duet: 'sends out two blades which converge on each other. Enemies caught in between are damaged, stunned and Marked'

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers say 'trade around Flawless Duet's cooldown' without giving it, and mid asserts a window exists 'between her W and her E stun timer' with no numbers behind it.
audit.why: Flawless Duet is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s and Defiant Dance is 20/18/16/14/12s — at the levels the mid text is describing (4-5) those are the two longest cooldowns she owns, versus Bladesurge at 10/9/8/7/6 which effectively never goes down because it refreshes off Marked targets. That is the honest shape of the window and it is worth stating.
audit.corrected: 16s rank-1 Flawless Duet is the number to track; Bladesurge is not a cooldown you can wait out.
sources: champ-data/_kits/irelia.json — E cooldown 16/14.5/13/11.5/10, W 20/18/16/14/12, Q 10/9/8/7/6 with refresh clause

audit.whatIsWrong: mid and late route the level-6 and late-game plan through "Abyssal Voyage" — "your Abyssal Voyage now gives you global threat" and "use Abyssal Voyage to threaten global flanks".
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the pre-2021-rework ultimate and does not exist on the live champion. Tahm Kench has no global. Against Irelia specifically this error is compounding: the entry tells the player his answer to her level-6 spike is to leave the lane and pressure the map, when in reality he has no way to leave and — per the point above — no way to escape her R wall either.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is Devour, gated at three An Acquired Taste stacks. The entry tool is Abyssal Dive.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — W Abyssal Dive, R Devour, no global ability

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your clearest dueling window in this lane: Irelia has no meaningful defensive cooldown between her W and her E stun timer, and if you have 3 An Acquired Taste stacks ready, a stun into empowered Devour removes her from the fight for the full hold duration with bonus damage — she cannot Riposte it and she cannot dash out. Use this window to deny CS and burn her Summoner spells. At 6 her all-in confidence spikes again because she can chain Q resets and her shred is compounding, so respect her burst window and play around cooldowns; your Abyssal Voyage now gives you global threat and lets you stay relevant on the map rather than sitting in a losing trade pattern.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your clearest dueling window in this lane: Irelia's only defensive cooldown is Defiant Dance and it reduces physical damage, so if you have 3 An Acquired Taste stacks ready, a stun into Devour removes her from the fight for the full hold duration — her W does nothing to that magic damage and she cannot dash out. Use this window to deny CS and burn her Summoner spells. At 6 her all-in confidence spikes again because Bladesurge refreshes off Marked targets and Ionian Fervor is at full stacks, so respect her burst window and play around cooldowns; your own 6 is Devour, and it still needs three stacks on her before you can cast it at all.

edits.before: Two items in, Irelia's shred and sustained damage can no longer burst you fast enough to avoid your Thick Skin grey-health banking, and Devour still removes her clean from a teamfight — point-and-click lockdown does not care how much mobility she has once your 3 stacks are up. Peel your carries with Devour and use Abyssal Voyage to threaten global flanks. The one thing that still kills you late is her getting a lead and compounding shred from a stacked passive before you can Tongue Lash from range — never let her free-reset Q through your whole backline.
edits.after: Two items in, Irelia's on-hit damage can no longer burst you fast enough to avoid your Thick Skin grey-health banking, and Devour still removes her clean from a teamfight — point-and-click lockdown does not care how much mobility she has once your 3 stacks are up. Peel your carries with Devour and enter with Abyssal Dive. The one thing that still kills you late is Vanguard's Edge: its wall cuts the retreat you have no dash to make, so hold Flash for the wall and never let her free-reset Bladesurge through your backline.

notes: "she cannot Riposte it" is a cross-champion contamination — Riposte is Fiora's W and has been pasted into an Irelia entry. That suggests the generator was reusing a Fiora-shaped template, so it is worth grepping champ-data for other champions' ability names appearing in matchups they do not belong to (Riposte, Riftwalk, Meditate and similar signature names are good probes). Note this class of error, like Abyssal Voyage and Cruel Tide, is invisible to the packet's suspectNames detector, which only scores near-miss spellings against the CORRECT champion's kit and will happily pass a perfectly-spelled ability belonging to someone else. Level-chart mismatch persists here too: content win has Irelia ahead at 3, 6 and first item while full phases[].side has Tahm Kench ahead at 3, first item and 2+items.
